resources.string: Heartline is a wellness app. It can\'t diagnose, treat or rule out any condition. If you feel unwell, contact a doctor or emergency services.
Your watch checks your rhythm in the background while you\'re still.
Open Heartline on your watch and choose ECG.
Rest your arm on a table and sit still.
Hold your fingertip lightly on the top key for 30 seconds.
Your heart beat in a uniform pattern between 50 and 100 bpm. This is the pattern usually seen in a normally beating heart.
Your heart beat in an irregular pattern. This can be a sign of atrial fibrillation (AFib). If you haven\'t been told you have AFib, talk to your doctor.
Your heart rate was over 120 bpm, so the rhythm couldn\'t be checked. Exercise, stress, alcohol or dehydration can raise your heart rate.
Your heart rate was under 50 bpm, so the rhythm couldn\'t be checked. Some medicines and very good fitness can lower your heart rate.
The recording couldn\'t be classified. Make sure your arm is resting and try again.
Too much noise was detected. Rest your arm on a table, keep still and touch the key lightly.
Recordings you take on your watch appear here, with the full waveform and a PDF you can share.
It will also be removed from your watch.
Add any symptoms you had while recording. They are included in your report.
Single lead (Lead I) · 25 mm/s · 10 mm/mV · %1$d Hz · Recorded with a Galaxy Watch and Heartline
Your watch measures your heart rate in the background and sends it here every 15 minutes.
You\'ll see irregular rhythm and high or low heart rate notifications here.
Notifications are checks, not a diagnosis. Your watch looks for an irregular rhythm only while you\'re still, and can\'t detect heart attacks, blood clots or stroke.
Your heart showed signs of an irregular rhythm. Take an ECG and talk to your doctor if this continues.
Your heart rate was above %1$d bpm for 10 minutes while you seemed inactive.
Your heart rate was below %1$d bpm for 10 minutes while you seemed inactive.
Your watch estimates blood pressure from your pulse. It needs 3 readings from a cuff every 4 weeks.
Blood pressure from your watch is an estimate based on your calibration. It can\'t replace a cuff, and it isn\'t meant to diagnose hypertension.
Have an upper-arm blood pressure cuff ready.
Sit with your back supported and feet flat for 5 minutes.
Wear the cuff on one arm and your watch on the other wrist, both at heart level.
You\'ll take 3 readings, about a minute apart.
Stand up and wait one minute. Hold your watch arm across your chest at heart level, and keep the cuff arm relaxed at heart level too.
Recommended. One more reading while standing shows Heartline how your pulse and pressure respond when you get up, so a racing pulse after standing isn\'t mistaken for high pressure.
Some conditions and medicines change how your pulse wave relates to blood pressure. Heartline adjusts its estimate to them. Stored only with your calibration.
I take a beta blocker or another heart-rate medicine
I have POTS or my pressure drops when I stand
I have diabetes or kidney disease
Start your cuff now. Heartline opens on your watch and starts measuring by itself. Keep still until both finish.
Type the values shown on your cuff.
Check the values: systolic 70–250, diastolic 40–150, systolic above diastolic.
You can measure blood pressure on your watch for the next 4 weeks.
Measure on your watch. Your results appear here with a trend and history.
Measure again to see a trend
Across: skeletal muscle · Up: body fat. Compared with people of your sex and age.
Low body fat and low muscle. Strength training and enough protein build muscle.
Low body fat with standard muscle.
Low body fat and more muscle than most: an athletic build.
Standard body fat but low muscle. Strength training would help.
Body fat and muscle are both in the standard range.
Standard body fat with more muscle than most.
More body fat and less muscle than standard, even at a normal weight. Activity and strength training help most.
Body fat is above the standard range, muscle is standard.
Both body fat and muscle are above standard.
How well your cells hold a charge, from the body\'s response to the tiny current. Higher usually means healthier cells and more muscle; it falls with age and illness.
Blood oxygen is measured with red and infrared light while you keep still. Readings of 95–100% are typical at rest. It isn\'t a medical oximeter.
Skin temperature changes with the room and your activity, so Heartline shows the change from your own 7-day baseline. It isn\'t body temperature.
Body composition uses a small electrical current between your wrist and fingers. Measure at the same time of day, before eating or exercising.
Stress is estimated from your heart rate variability over one minute at rest (and skin conductance on Galaxy Watch8). Lower is calmer.
Used to personalise Heartline and to estimate body composition on your watch. It stays on your devices.

Tap to pick the exact day you were born.
Body-composition formulas need a biological reference. It is used only for those calculations and is never shown anywhere. Skip it and everything except body composition still works.

Choose the option that fits you best, or “Prefer not to say”.

resources.string: Heartline records a single-lead ECG, estimates blood pressure after cuff calibration, and checks your heart rhythm in the background with a Galaxy Watch. It\'s for general wellness and to help you talk with your doctor.

Heartline isn\'t a medical device. It can\'t diagnose, treat or rule out any condition, and it can\'t detect heart attacks, blood clots or stroke. Don\'t change your medication or treatment based on it. If you think you\'re having a medical emergency, call emergency services.
Measurements stay on your watch and phone. There\'s no account, no server, no analytics and no ads. Data only leaves your devices when you share or export it.

Heartline reads your watch\'s ECG, heart-rate, PPG and other sensors through Samsung\'s Health Platform (Health Sensor Service). Apps that aren\'t distributed by Samsung partners can only do that while the Health Platform\'s developer mode is on. It takes about 30 seconds and you only do it once.
On your watch, open Settings (swipe down from the watch face and tap the gear icon).
Find and tap Health Platform (Health Sensor Service). If you don\'t see it, tap “See all apps” or “App info” first.
On the Health Platform screen, quickly tap the “Health Platform” title at the top about 10 times in a row.
When “[Dev mode]” appears under the title, developer mode is on. If a confirmation appears, tap OK.
Go back to Heartline on your watch and tap “Check again” at the bottom of the help page.
Tapping the title 10 times again turns developer mode off. A watch software update can turn it off too; Heartline will tell you if that happens.

Very high. Check with a cuff. With chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness or trouble speaking or seeing, get help now.
Low. Check with a cuff. If you feel dizzy or faint, sit or lie down.

Fast pulse with a weak wrist pulse: weighted towards transit time rather than pulse shape.
Irregular rhythm: averaged over more beats.
Recommended. Keep a finger on the watch\'s lower key during each reading, so the ECG and motion channels are calibrated too.
